svg.text: TriageAgent explained: what each part does, why it is needed, and how it is built
Agent 1 of 6 · the first check after an alarm: is this a real leak, a false alarm, or is it unclear? · plain words for everyone, technical details for those who want them
Each card: WHAT IT IS and WHY IT IS NEEDED in plain words, then UNDER THE HOOD (grey strip) with the technical details · read the numbers 1 → 12 in order
A pressure sensor in the pipe network
reports that the pressure fell below its
limit. An operator starts the check (later
an alarm can start it by itself).
On its own an alarm cannot tell a burst
pipe from planned valve work or a busy
hour. Someone has to look at the
context first: that is this agent’s job.

The one way in and out of the agent: a
web address that the workflow calls
The workflow hands in the alarm and
gets a checked answer back. Only a
caller with the key gets in.

Every alarm is checked in the same
careful way, like a written procedure. It
also says: never guess a number, and
all the facts the agent collected. On its
own it knows nothing about Evides.

writes a short explanation a duty
manager can read. It does not decide

A fixed form the agent must fill in: the verdict, how sure it is, a

Software can read a form, not a story, so code can check every
TriageVerdict: typed JSON answer schema, set at
Above: a real answer of the burst run, shortened
Fixed rules in ordinary software that check the model’s answer against
A second pair of eyes. The answer must quote the alarm sensor’s own
readings and have enough evidence, or it becomes “unclear”. A false
alarm is only accepted when the planned-works list really shows work
going on: closing a real leak would be the worst mistake. When the rules
overrule the model, it gets one more try.

and the alarm sensor with a reading in bar or m³/h; otherwise
Overruled → 1 retry; the second answer stands
itself; false_alarm only with an active, not completed work

The burst example in plain words (a real run of the demo)
At night the pressure at one sensor fell from 4.89 to 2.85 bar, while the water flowing into the district rose to 121 m³/h: normal for that hour is at most about 48. There
was no planned work. The agent looked up 9 facts and sources and concluded “genuine leak”, 96% sure, in about 17 seconds. The rules agreed, so the next agent took
ALM-2026-1114-0001 · PS-101 4.89 → 2.85 bar in 3 h · inflow FS-101 121 m³/h, p95 for this hour 48.4 · no planned works
9 calls: list-sensors, get-sensor-readings ×4, get-planned-works, get-weather, get-usage-history, knowledge_base_retrieve
9,365 + 1,120 tokens · 17.0 s · genuine_leak 0.96 → diagnose · captured 2026-11-16 from the deployed demo
Instructions = how to work · Tools = facts · Knowledge = experience · Skill = habit · Form = readable by software · Code + a person = safe
All data is simulated, not a real Evides system · resource group rg-evides-ai-demo · registered by LeakOps.AgentRegistry · the technical version of this picture is docs/architecture-triage-agent.png
